digest.key_takeaway:
A model reports 0.84 mean average precision (mAP) on your benchmark test set. Management approves deployment, and marketing drafts the launch announcement.

Three days later, field reports arrive: the model is failing systematically. In crowded retail aisles, busy warehouse loading docks, or messy construction sites, false detections proliferate and target objects are repeatedly missed.

The failure is not that the model suddenly degraded. The failure is that aggregate mAP told only half the story.

articles.title: The AI Labs' Public Pacing Calls Are Now Antitrust Evidence
articles.summary:

articles.title: Parallel coding agents, one human: how to stop being the bottleneck
articles.summary:
Starting four coding agents is the easy part. Then the first one asks to run the tests, the second has a question about the cache, the third says it's done, and the fourth has been waiting on you for ten minutes in a tab you haven't looked at. Run agents in parallel without a plan for your own attention, and it mostly means waiting in parallel.

You are the one part of the setup that doesn't scale, so the work is in asking less of yourself. Here's what does that, in plain tools first, then the same thing in a desktop app.

articles.title: Angular's TypeScript 7-Powered Compiler Enters Beta with Rust-Based Preprocessor
articles.summary: The Angular team has introduced ngp, a compiler preprocessor that rewrites the analysis stage in Rust using Oxc. It replaces ngc's dependence on the Transformer API, which TypeScript 7.0 removed. An early benchmark showed 2x to 3x faster cold builds. Adoption is expected in an Angular 22 minor release; production builds should stay on ngc until then. By Daniel Curtis

articles.title: Waiting, Not Computing: The Real Reason Your CPU is Maxed Out
articles.summary:

The resource calculator tells you there is plenty of headroom, but in reality, the server is choking. articles.summary:

articles.summary:
Trained on six PathMNIST tissues with a small KEEP adapter, it handled added labels without retraining, though a linear classifier hit 88% on familiar ones.

articles.title: PSI is trying to make a business out of AI-driven scientific discovery
articles.summary: PSI used an unreleased Anthropic model to answer a fundamental question about quantum computing that scientists have pursued for nearly two decades.

articles.title: Anthropic launches Claude Meetings to turn workplace discussions into plans and tasks
articles.summary: As participants talk, Claude can draft the plan being discussed, map out a timeline on a whiteboard, answer questions in the meeting chat, and access connected work apps to retrieve information, such as last year's figures.

articles.title: OpenAI rolls out new business profiles, making ChatGPT just a little bit more like Google
articles.summary: OpenAI is looking to make ChatGPT a more robust consumer discovery engine, and a host of new features seek to empower businesses to help it do that.

articles.title: OpenAI acquires Odessia, travel startup created by Sonder founder
articles.summary: OpenAI has not yet said what its plans are for the future of travel. But Sonder founder Francis Davidson is a well-known figure in the travel industry.

articles.title: Cloudflare Makes Basin Serverless Analytics Generally Available
articles.summary: Cloudflare has announced the general availability of Basin, a serverless analytics platform built on Apache Iceberg and R2 Object Storage. The managed service supports open data formats and integrates with tools such as DuckDB, Snowflake, and Apache Spark, with no data egress fees. By Renato Losio

articles.summary: Autark can act without constant prompting, but leaves users to enforce their own security boundaries

articles.title: After challenging Google’s Android with Cyanogen, its co-founder takes aim at Windows for AI era
articles.summary: Kora is set to launch as a free-to-use alternative to Windows, targeting users who rely heavily on AI models and agents.

articles.summary:

The post Scikit-Learn Matched or Beat Jev's Calibration on BANKING77 appeared first on Towards Data Science.

articles.title: Cyberattacks threaten to make open source AI a little less open, Hugging Face exec warns
articles.summary: Hugging Face executive Irene Solaiman warns that growing cyberattacks on open AI platforms could force tighter security restrictions, threatening the accessibility that makes open source communities valuable to developers worldwide.

articles.title: A Session-Start Hook Raised Claude Code Skill Firing From 15% to 62%
articles.summary:
A software tester ran six testing skills on Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus; pushy descriptions added only 5 points, and near-miss requests never fired a skill.
The post A Session-Start Hook Raised Claude Code Skill Firing From 15% to 62% appeared first on Towards Data Science.

articles.title: I benchmarked TimesFM 3.0, Chronos-2 and Toto 2.0 on market time series. None beat simple baseline. [P]
articles.summary: I may be naive, but I've been curious whether the recent wave of time-series foundation models can actually extract useful predictive signals from financial markets. Models like Google's TimesFM 3.0, Amazon's Chronos-2, and Datadog's Toto 2.0 are impressive general-purpose forecasters from the first sight.
